en.title: Hyphenation: Keep a Single Consonant
en.summary: A single consonant between two vowels always moves to the next syllable when you speak and when you write.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs:
You divide spoken words into syllables.
A syllable is one beat of a word.
A consonant is a sound you make when your mouth narrows the air.
A vowel is a sound you make with open air in your mouth.
One consonant between two vowels always joins the second syllable.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs:
Listen to (ma-mă) /ˈma.mə/, which means mother.
The first beat ends after the vowel.
You close your lips for the middle consonant.
You open your lips for the second beat.
You do not hold the sound in the first beat.
You send the consonant to the next syllable cleanly.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs:
A letter is a written sign of the alphabet.
You split words between syllables at the end of a line.
A single consonant letter between two vowels belongs to the second syllable.
You write (ma-mă) /ˈma.mə/ with a hyphen after the first vowel.
The consonant begins the second part on the next line.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs:
Do not connect the middle consonant to the first syllable.
Some learners keep the sound in the first beat.
That makes a double consonant.
A double consonant is a consonant that you hold longer, or say twice.
Keep the first vowel free of that sound.
Say (ma-mă) /ˈma.mə/ without any pause in the middle.
